messages:
jordan: FYI incoming high-priority support ticket from AcmePay. They report sudden 500s from the hosted API (/v1/generate and /v1/embeddings). They expect 429 when they exceed quota but are getting 500s. Started ~09:12Z; lots of downstream errors and some billing spikes. Ticket: #4357.
ryan: assigning myself. can you paste a sample request-id / headers / approximate QPS when it started?
jordan: sample from their logs: 
```
request_id=01H7XJZK2A sample_id=ab12
method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=500 latency=1223ms
resp_body="quota-orchestrator: dependency timeout" x-upstream-timeout=11000ms x-quota-route=rate-orch-3
```
They said burst was ~80 QPS, baseline ~20 QPS.
ashley: any correlation in our metrics? is this a capacity thing or classification error? :thinking_face:
devin: looking at tracing now. I see a pattern: quota-orchestrator calls quota-classifier which in some host pools is returning 504/timeouts to the gateway. The gateway then bubbles that up as 500 instead of converting to a 429.
ryan: that sounds like the misroute we've seen before — dependency timeout turned into opaque 5xx. need to confirm if the router fell back to a non-rate-limited path.
devin: digging deeper. trace sample: 
```
trace_id=trc-9a7
gateway->quota-orch (10ms)
quota-orch->kv-redis (10.8s) TIMED_OUT
quota-orch returns 500 -> gateway returns 500
```
So the orchestrator is timing out on calls to our KV store (cluster-us-east-2).
maria: this is customer-impacting. AcmePay is on a paid Dedicated plan, SLA request inbound. Support is asking for an ETA.
jordan: I told them we're investigating and will update in 15m. they reported 09:12Z as start.
ryan: immediate mitigation options: 1) short-term: patch gateway to map quota-orch dependency timeouts to a 429 with header to indicate fallback, 2) roll traffic to healthy quota-orch pool, 3) increase quota timeouts on gateway to tolerate slower KV but that risks higher p99 latency.
ashley: do we have healthy pools to shift to? If the KV cluster itself is degraded, rolling might not help.
devin: cluster-us-east-2 shows elevated op latencies and some node evictions. I'm seeing spikes in pod restarts. probable cause: a recent config change bumped connection pools. I'll open an infra ticket.
ryan: while infra works on KV, I want the quick mitigation that reduces customer 500s -> convert to 429 so apps don't explode and billing logic remains sane. can we hotfix the gateway handler to treat quota-orch 504/timeouts as 429?
devin: yes, we can add a mapping in the quota-gateway error handler. patch small. I'll build and canary to 1 host in us-east-2.
deploy-bot: build started: quota-gateway v2.14.3-hotfix-mapper (ci/5482).
ryan: thx. jordan, please add request ids from AcmePay to the support ticket and ask them for a reproducible curl if possible.
jordan: sent a reply asking for curl and headers. they provided a repro snippet: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"test"}' &
done
wait
```
They say first batch triggers the 500s.
devin: test repro locally against canary — I can reproduce consistent 500s if I force quota-orch into the timeout path.
ryan: deploy the patch to canary, monitor 5xx rate and 429s, and only promote if mapping behaves as expected. we want gateway to return 429 + header `x-quota-mapped: timeout->429` so customers see rate limit semantics.
devin: deploying canary to host id=us-east-2-gw-07 now.
(10m passes)
devin: canary up. initial telemetry: requests that previously returned 500 now return 429 with header. 5xx rate dropped by ~86% for the canary host.
jordan: AcmePay confirms fewer 500s for requests routed to the canary IP. They still see some 500s — likely hitting hosts without the patch.
ryan: progressive roll. promote to 20% traffic, monitor error budgets.
sre-bot: Alert: quota-orch downstream KV latency > 10s in us-east-2 (alert_id=AL-7832).
ashley: infra, can you check why KV latency spiked? any config changes in the last 2 hours?
devin: infra says operator restarted a node earlier to apply kernel patch. connection pools didn't drain fully. I'm coordinating safe restarts and pool tuning.
maria: comms: I'm drafting a status update for AcmePay and the status page. will state mitigation steps and ETA for full remediations.
ryan: long-term we need: 1) more conservative default for dependency timeouts mapping, 2) better classifier in quota-orch to fail-open with 429 semantics on KV hiccups, 3) infra runbook to gracefully drain connection pools on restarts.
devin: opened GH issues: RW-issue-981 (gateway mapping), RW-issue-982 (quota-orch failopen), RW-issue-983 (kv pool drain).
jordan: support updated AcmePay with canary result and asked for any remaining request_ids. they acknowledged and will monitor for 2 hours.
ryan: final action items and owners:
- ryan: promote hotfix to 100% in 30m if error rates stay low (ETA 30m).
- devin: follow infra KV recovery and validate no more timeouts (ETA 45m).
- ashley: coordinate postmortem and SLO impact calc (ETA EOD).
- maria: customer comms + support ticket summary (ETA 20m).
- jordan: keep the ticket updated and collect customer request_ids (ongoing).
deploy-bot: canary promoted to 20% (ci/5482).
(20m)
devin: KV cluster recovered; op latencies trending normal. nodes stabilized. all quota-orch pods healthy.
ryan: promoting to 100% now.
deploy-bot: rollout to 100% completed (ci/5482).
jordan: AcmePay says errors have subsided; their app returned to normal and billing anomaly resolved.
maria: good. we'll schedule a postmortem. please capture traces and timeline.
ashley: I'll open the incident postmortem doc and add notes from this thread.
ryan: closing loop: mapping fix reduced customer impact quickly, infra fix prevents recurrence. follow-up items in GH RW-issue-981/982/983.
jordan: closing ticket after 2h of stability. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
